acts.inspired_by: the schoolhouse test story (2026-09-26): a line the pass read as pride
context: The magistrate asked Kit a question and Kit turned to you instead of answering.
acts.act: You said: "Look at Mr. Holt. He asked you a question."

context: The captain is holding the lamp over the wounded man while you work.
acts.act: You said: "Gauze, Captain. Hold it ready."

context: A traveller asks you when the next train to the coast leaves.
Your son is heading out into the cold without his coat.
A traveller reaches your post at the gate.
A printer's proof of the programme is set on the music rest in front of you.
acts.act: You did: lower your pince-nez and read the printed page.

acts.inspired_by: the schoolhouse test story: a boy clears the teacher who lied for him -- a claim that may itself be a lie told for someone, so mixed, not scored
context: Your teacher lied to the magistrate to protect you, and the lie is now on the record.
acts.act: You said: "Write down that Miss Oldis only said what she did because I asked her to."

acts.inspired_by: courage under fire (the Victoria Cross citations)
context: Brenner is down in the open ground, and the enemy guns are still firing.
acts.act: You did: run out, haul Brenner onto your shoulders and carry him back to the trench under fire.

acts.inspired_by: speaking up at a cost (whistleblowing research, Near and Miceli)
context: In front of the whole board, your boss presents figures you know are false.
acts.act: You said: "Those numbers are wrong, sir. I checked them twice."

acts.inspired_by: the lost wallet experiments (Cohn et al., 2019)
acts.who: Ada, a cleaner who is behind on her rent
context: You found a wallet with a month's wages in it on the train.
acts.act: You did: hand the wallet, money untouched, to its owner at the lost-property desk.

acts.inspired_by: rescue at risk of one's own life
context: Everyone is out of the burning house except the youngest child.
acts.act: You did: go back into the smoke and bring the child out.

acts.inspired_by: the schoolhouse test story: an honest woman lies to a magistrate
acts.who: Margit, a schoolteacher who has never told a lie in twenty years
context: The magistrate asks whether Kit Sawyer is here; Kit is hiding behind the door.
acts.act: You said: "Kit Sawyer is not in this room."

acts.inspired_by: the fort test story: a captain betrays his garrison
context: The enemy's messenger is waiting for this week's patrol times.
acts.act: You did: write out the patrol routes in your own hand and seal the letter for the enemy.

acts.inspired_by: losing one's temper with a child
context: Your four-year-old has been crying for an hour and will not stop.
acts.act: You did: slap her across the face.

context: Your friend left her purse open on the table and went to the kitchen.
acts.act: You did: take two notes from her purse and slip them into your pocket.

context: Brenner is down in the open ground, calling your name, and the guns are firing.
acts.act: You did: turn and run for the trench, leaving him there.

acts.inspired_by: one cruel act, two kinds of people
context: A beggar sits by the station steps with a tin cup of coins.
acts.act: You did: kick the beggar's cup across the street and laugh.

context: A beggar sits by the station steps with a tin cup of coins.
acts.act: You did: kick the beggar's cup across the street and laugh.

context: You have just won the regional chess final.
acts.act: You said: "Of course I won. Nobody in this room could have beaten me."
